electric-charges-fields-and-gausss-law-p: Rub a balloon and it becomes charged. Where did that charge come from?
Halve the distance between two charges. How many times bigger does the force between them get?
Field lines are just drawn on paper. How can their spacing tell you how strong a force is?
Charge a metal ball. Where does the extra charge end up, and what is the field inside the metal?
At the center of a charged ring the field is zero. Why not a little way along its axis?
A charge sits inside a closed box of any shape. Why is the total flux out of the box always the same?
Inside a uniformly charged ball, does the field get stronger or weaker toward the center?
electric-potential: If the electric field at a point is zero, must the electric potential there be zero too?
Released from rest among equipotential lines, which way does an electron move, and does it speed up?
Bend a charged rod into a half circle. Why is the potential at its center so easy to find?
A charged wire runs on forever. Why can't its potential be zero infinitely far away?
An electron and a proton feel the same force between charged plates. Which swerves more, and by how much?
conductors-and-capacitors: Two metal spheres, one big and one small, are joined by a wire. Which ends up with more charge?
A charged capacitor has no net charge at all. So what is it actually storing?
How can you get more charge onto a capacitor without raising the voltage?
Make a capacitor twice as big in every direction. How much more charge does it store per volt?
electric-circuits-part-1: A lamp glows while charge flows through it. Does any of the charge get used up on the way?
A battery is marked one and a half volts, a lamp six. What exactly does a volt count?
Double the potential difference across a wire. When does the current exactly double?
Stretch a metal wire to twice its length. What happens to its resistance?
A rod conducts less well toward one end. Where along it is the electric field strongest?
One dead bulb can put out a whole string of lights, yet home lamps work on their own. Why?
electric-circuits-part-2: Go once round any loop of a circuit. Why do the rises and drops in potential always cancel?

Why do a car's headlights dim while its starter motor is turning?

magnetic-fields-and-electromagnetism: Switch on a current in a wire just above a compass. Which way does the needle turn, and why?
A magnet grabs an iron nail but ignores a copper pipe. What is different inside the iron?

A magnetic field can steer a beam of charged particles. Can it also make them go faster?

Why is the field at a wire loop's center about three times that at the same distance from a straight wire?
Why does the field inside a long solenoid not depend on the solenoid's radius at all?

Move a metal rod or spin a coil near a magnet, and a voltage appears. What decides how big it is?

How can a straight line expose a law that is hiding inside a curve?

Why do physicists time 20 swings of a pendulum instead of just one?
